newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips ease pulling SAX index lower.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips ease pulling SAX index lower.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mostly lower in listless trading on Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, dragging the SAX index down 0.58 points to 208.65.
Brokers characterised trading as uneventful, with a lack of new investors, and low activity by current players adding to the bourse's sluggishness.
Oil and gas storage firm Nafta was the biggest decliner on the index, closing down 59 crowns at 2,001, though brokers said the share now had a more realistic market price.
Slovakia's largest commercial bank, VUB, lost five crowns to close at 1,830, with its average price - according to which the index is calculated - easing by 1.03 percent.
"There is domestic interest in purchasing VUB share at around 1,800 crowns, where the price should gradually fall," said said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt
Oil refiner Slovnaft did not trade on Wednesday, after closing at 935 crowns on Tuesday.
"There are enough offers to sell Slovnaft share, but at a rather higher prices than the current level," Briska added.
Overall volume fell to 111,520 shares traded on Wednesday, from 203,036 shares on Tuesday, turnover decreased to 98.32 million crowns after 417.60 million on Tuesday.
